title: pedicularis lutescens subsp. ramosa
intro: Pedicularis lutescens subsp. ramosa, commonly known as  a type of flowering plant in the family Orobanchaceae. It is a parasitic plant that obtains its nutrients by connecting to the roots of other plants. Pedicularis lutescens subsp. ramosa is used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues, due to its potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of this plant include iridoids, phenolic acids, and flavonoids, which are believed to exhibit therapeutic actions such as sedative, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects.
